articles.title: Democrats Win US House and Senate
articles.intro: Explore how Democrats captured both chambers of the US Congress, voter frustrations, diverse historic wins, and the impact on President Trump's term.

sentences.text: Democrats have won control of both chambers of the US Congress, as voters expressed their dissatisfaction with Washington under the control of Republicans and President Donald Trump.
The country's November 3 midterm elections exposed voters' frustrations over high prices, the Iran war and concerns over government corruption.
Democrats won across the map, flipping states that had voted Republican for decades and that Trump won easily just two years ago.
That includes James Talarico's Senate victory in Texas, where no Democrat had won statewide office in more than 30 years.

The election also delivered the country's first Muslim senator, first Native American female senator and first openly gay male senator, as well as the country’s first Black female governor and first Native female governor.
Young people and Latinos, who helped return Trump to the White House two years ago, are now moving away from Republicans, according to The AP Voter Poll, a survey of midterm voters in all 50 states.

The AP Voter Poll also showed that about three-quarters of voters feel "angry" or "dissatisfied" with the country's direction, while about 6 in 10 see Trump as prioritizing his personal interests over those of the country.
The president's failure to deliver on key promises — particularly to reduce inflation, which has worsened instead — also held back his fellow Republicans.
Democrats increased their support with moderate voters, particularly in key Senate races where Democrats flipped Republican-held seats.
About 8 in 10 moderate voters said Congress was not doing enough to provide checks and balances on the president.
It was all a major blow to Trump, who spent nearly every day of the last month speaking in front of supporters, telling voters to "pretend I'm on the ballot."
As the results came in, Trump blamed individual Republican candidates for their losses, though he also said Democrats "did a good job."
Trump now faces a very changed Washington for the last two years of his presidency.
Democrats will have the power to block laws he supports, reject his choices for key positions and investigate his government.

articles.title: Japan Launches New Agency to Deal with Disasters
articles.intro: Learn about Japan’s new disaster agency, its role in preparing for future earthquakes, tsunamis, and how it aims to improve emergency shelters.

sentences.text: Japan has launched a new disaster management agency to improve the country's preparedness for major earthquakes, tsunamis and volcanic eruptions.
The National Disaster Management Agency, which began operating on November 2, has more than 350 staff members responsible for disaster preparedness, emergency response and reconstruction efforts.
Japan, which lies along the Pacific "Ring of Fire," is one of the world's most disaster-prone countries but has never had an agency dedicated to disaster management.
Instead, the country has relied on temporary response teams assembled from different government ministries and departments.

As part of the launch, the agency urged local governments and residents to check the quake resistance of their homes, make sure their furniture is safely anchored, evaluate their evacuation procedures and stock up on emergency supplies.

The agency was not established in response to any specific threat, but amid concerns about Japan's ability to cope with another crisis on the scale of the 2011 quake and tsunami, which killed nearly 20,000 people, and triggered the Fukushima nuclear disaster.
Experts have warned of the possibility of major quakes in the coming decades and officials want people to be prepared.
The biggest worry is a megaquake along the Nankai Trough, an undersea trench off Japan's southeastern coast.
According to government estimates, such a disaster could kill 298,000 people, force 6.5 million to evacuate and destroy 2.35 million homes.

A major earthquake in metropolitan Tokyo could cause another 18,000 deaths, while an eruption of Mount Fuji could affect 790,000 people and disrupt transportation, power lines and other infrastructure.

Japan has long been criticized for its poorly equipped evacuation centers, where people are typically crowded into gymnasiums, community centers and classrooms that lack adequate privacy, bedding, clean toilets or hot food.
The new agency aims to change that by bringing in clean portable toilets, kitchens serving hot food, bathing facilities and cardboard beds.

The importance of better shelters became clear after the 2011 disaster, when {{prn:3,810|three thousand eight hundred and ten}} people died from causes linked to harsh living conditions following the earthquake and tsunami.

articles.title: UK Airline Offers to Pay for Babies' First Passports
articles.intro: Learn about a UK airline offering to cover the cost of babies' first passports, parental travel experiences, and family vacation milestones.

sentences.text: The end of September is the busiest time for births in the UK.
And with so many new babies in the country, one company is already hoping to turn some of them into customers — and get them on a plane!

British airline and vacation company Easyjet has announced that it will cover the cost of a child's passport when new parents book a trip — or, at least, give parents a discount that will cover the passport cost.
Until November 26, 2026, parents of babies will be able to save about $90 on Easyjet trips, which is the same as the price of a child's first passport in the UK.
They can use the offer once per vacation booking for one child up to 2 years old.
Easyjet also surveyed 2,000 British parents who had taken a child under 5 on vacation at least once about their experiences.
Four out of five parents said their baby's first vacation was a "landmark family moment," with 57% saying it was one of their proudest parenting milestones.
They were also asked about the difficult parts of organizing international travel with a new baby.
And nearly one in 10 said they didn't even know their baby needed their own passport before they started planning their vacation!
Parents also said it took an average of four tries to get a passport picture approved for their baby — after all, you can't tell a baby how to pose for a photo!
Still, 48% said their baby's first vacation was easier than they had expected, and 87% said they felt good about doing it all again.
Also, even though 27% said they thought it would be difficult for small children to adapt to a new routine on vacation, 50% said their children were actually able to do so quite well.

articles.title: Sardinian Restaurants Ask Families to Put Phones Away
articles.intro: This lesson explores Sardinian restaurants asking families to put away electronic devices at meals to encourage conversation and quality time together.

sentences.text: Going out for a meal with your family should be a chance to enjoy good food and spend time together.
But these days, it's common to see everyone looking at their phones or watching videos on tablets instead of talking.
Now, some restaurants on the Italian island of Sardinia are trying to change that.

Starting in early November, 15 restaurants are encouraging parents and children to put away their phones and other electronic devices during meals, so they can spend more time talking and enjoying their meals together.
The project, called "At the Table Without Screens," will run for one month at first, and more restaurants may join later.
Families visiting these restaurants can choose whether to take part in the project.
Those who agree are asked to leave their devices in their bags or put them in a basket at the table.
But the restaurants aren't just asking families to stop using their phones — they're also giving them something else to do.
Families receive a special kit with games, drawing activities and other things to help parents and children talk more.
They can play games while waiting for their food, or use the activities as a starting point for conversations.
The kit also includes advice for parents on children's screen time and social media use at home.
The project is led by Anna Cau, Sardinia's children's ombudsman.
She believes parents need more support to help their children use technology safely.
Emanuele Frongia, the head of a restaurant association in Sardinia, says dining out should be a time for families to talk and enjoy each other's company.
"But adults must set a good example first," he said.
"We can't ask children to put away their phones if we're not willing to do the same."

articles.title: 80% of Netflix Users Have Watched Korean Content
articles.intro: Explore the global rise of Korean dramas on Netflix, their international popularity, and how subtitles and dubbing boost their worldwide appeal.

sentences.text: Have you ever watched a Korean drama on Netflix?
If you have, you're certainly not alone!
According to Netflix, about 80% of its subscribers around the world have watched at least one Korean show or movie.
It's been 10 years since Netflix arrived in South Korea in 2016.
And since then, Korean entertainment has become popular in many different parts of the world.
Since 2021, Netflix has shared weekly lists of its 10 most-watched shows and movies around the world, called the "Global Top 10."
More than 210 different Korean shows and movies have appeared on these lists.
One of the biggest hits has been _Squid Game_.
The series stayed on Netflix's Global Top 10 for 32 weeks, including nine weeks at number one.
But it's not just _Squid Game_ that's getting attention from people around the world.
In Japan, _Crash Landing on You_, a 2019 story about a South Korean woman who falls in love with a North Korean soldier, stayed in the country's Top 10 for 72 weeks.
In Bolivia, the 2009 show _Boys Over Flowers_ spent 49 weeks in the Top 10, while 2021's _Vincenzo_ stayed in Pakistan's Top 10 for 45 weeks.
One reason these shows have become so popular is that they're available in different languages.
For example, the third season of _Squid Game_, released in 2025, was available with subtitles in 37 languages.
People could also watch dubbed versions of the show in 24 languages.
So 10 years after Netflix arrived in South Korea, Korean entertainment is popular in countries all over the world.

articles.title: 1 in 10 Malaysian Men Borrow Money to Pay for Dates
articles.intro: This lesson explores a survey on dating costs in Malaysia, including who pays, popular date spots, and how rising expenses impact relationships.

sentences.text: You buy flowers and you pick up your date.
Then you go for dinner and have a few drinks.
It's the perfect date — but perhaps not for your wallet!
Dating can be expensive — and a new survey has found that more than one in 10 Malaysian men have borrowed money to pay for dates.
The survey was done by LEGASI Research.
It looked at how people in Malaysia date, including how much they spend on dates, where they go and who pays.
Nearly 60% of men said they usually cover the cost of the date themselves — even with someone they're in a relationship with.
However, half of female participants said they prefer to take turns paying.
Shopping malls, restaurants and cafes were found to be the most popular places for dates.

Half of participants said they think dating has become too expensive, with a similar percentage saying they spend between about {{prn:$12.50|twelve dollars and fifty cents}} and $50 per date, mostly on food and drinks.
And 13% of men said they had borrowed money to pay for dates, compared with 5% of women.
However, more than 75% of participants — both men and women — said they would increase their spending to keep a relationship going.
The survey comes at a time when many people in Malaysia are struggling with the rising cost of living.
A different survey found that nearly one in four Malaysians aged 25 to 44 had delayed marriage or having a child — or decided not to get married or have a child at all — because of money struggles.

articles.title: These US Cities Spend the Most on Groceries
articles.intro: Explore which US cities spend the most and least on groceries, and how prices and household income affect grocery budgets.

sentences.text: Grocery prices are rising around the world.
There are many reasons for this, including rising fuel costs, climate change and global instability, and the exact rise in prices can be very different depending on where you live.
Finance app WalletHub has put together a list of cities where Americans are spending the most and least amount of their money on groceries.
It looked at the prices of 26 common grocery items across 100 of the largest US cities.
It added up the cost of those items and compared that with the average household income in each city, to see where people are spending the largest share of their money at the grocery store.
Detroit, Michigan, is at the top of the list, with residents needing to spend more than 4% of the city's average household income to buy the 26 common grocery items.
Fremont, California, has the lowest spending as a percentage of income, at less than 1%.
That doesn't mean Detroit has the highest overall prices, though.
Looking at the specific prices of those 26 grocery items, Detroit is actually just the 39th most expensive city.
However, the city has the lowest average annual household income in America, at just under $40,000 — while Fremont's is over $160,000.
This means people in Detroit have to spend a higher percentage of their income on groceries compared to people in higher-earning cities.
The situation is similar in Cleveland, Ohio, where residents spend the second-largest percentage of their income on groceries — just under 4%.
Cleveland actually has relatively low prices for a number of items on the grocery list, but it also has the second-lowest average household income, at just under $41,000 per year.
Birmingham, Alabama, is in third place, with residents needing to spend 3.5% of their average $46,000 income on groceries.

articles.title: Study Finds How a High-Calorie Diet May Affect the Brain
articles.intro: Explore recent research on how high-calorie diets can harm brain function, impact cognitive health, and what might reverse these effects.

sentences.text: We already know that high-calorie diets can cause obesity and are linked with illnesses like type 2 diabetes.
But there is growing evidence that these diets may affect healthy brain function as well.
Studies have, in particular, linked high-calorie diets with poorer cognitive performance and an increased risk of conditions like Alzheimer's disease.
To better understand what may be causing this, researchers from the Institute of Science Tokyo looked at the effect of a high-calorie diet on mice.
Their study, published in _Molecular Psychiatry_, revealed how a high-calorie diet could be linked to altered brain function and cognitive impairment.
The researchers fed mice a diet that was high in fat — which is incredibly calorie-dense — for either one or six weeks.
Then they compared the nerve cells of these mice with those that ate a normal diet.
They found that the mice on a high-fat diet had reduced levels of a protein called PQBP1 in their cerebral cortex — an area of the brain that supports cognitive functioning.
PQBP1 regulates the production of other proteins that are necessary for the brain's nerve cells to work properly.
When they looked closer, the researchers found that higher levels of insulin — a hormone that manages blood sugar levels — among the mice on a high-fat diet had restricted the production of PQBP1.
The result was an overall decline in healthy brain activity.
However, the researchers also found a way to reverse this damage, which may have positive implications for human health too.
Some mice that were fed a high-fat diet were also treated with pioglitazone, a drug used for diabetes management.
The researchers found that the medication brought PQBP1 levels back to normal, and improved cognitive function.
They also had success in using gene therapy to restore PQBP1 and fix brain function problems.
So, while the study revealed the potential dangers of a high-calorie diet for brain health, it also found possible effective approaches for treating some of the negative impacts.

articles.title: British Adventurer Finishes 28-Year Walk Around the World
articles.intro: Explore the story of Karl Bushby, who completed a 28-year, 50,000 km walk around the world, facing challenges, delays, and emotional reunions.

sentences.text: After 28 years, 50,000 kilometers and countless challenges, British adventurer Karl Bushby has finally completed his journey around the world — on foot.
The 57-year-old returned to his hometown of Hull, England, on November 2, where hundreds cheered him before an emotional reunion with his mother.
"Sorry to keep you waiting," he joked.
Bushby set out from Punta Arenas, Chile, on November 1, 1998, aged 29.
His rules were simple: no transport to move him forward, and no returning home until he had completed the journey.
Over the next 28 years, he traveled through 30 countries across four continents, facing dangerous terrain, extreme weather and lengthy delays.
In 2001, he made his way through the dangerous Darién Gap, a rugged region of jungle and mountains between South and Central America.
He was then jailed for 18 days after crossing a restricted border zone in Panama.
In 2006, he and fellow adventurer Dimitry Kieffer crossed the icy Bering Strait between Alaska and Russia.
Along the way, they encountered a polar bear, fell into freezing water and nearly lost their supplies.
They were later jailed for entering Russia illegally.
He also swam across the Caspian Sea and the English Channel.
Visa problems, the 2008 financial crisis and the COVID-19 pandemic caused years of delays.
Bushby originally thought his journey might take about five years, but he knew that was unrealistic.
"We suspected that it was 12 years plus," he said.
"But never in our wildest dreams would we ever have imagined 28 years."
Although Bushby had met up with family members during his travels, he hadn't seen his mother in 10 years.
He also reunited with his 36-year-old son, and met his 12-year-old granddaughter for the first time.
With his journey over, Bushby now faces the challenge of figuring out what to do next.
But there's plenty to keep him busy.
He has several speaking engagements planned, a second memoir on the way and a documentary about his adventure being made.

articles.title: Japan Changes Tax-Free Shopping Rules for Tourists
articles.intro: Learn about Japan’s new tax-free shopping rules for tourists, including how refunds work, reasons for the changes, and their impact on tourism.

sentences.text: Shopping in Japan has changed for foreign tourists.
Until recently, tourists could buy many products without paying Japan's consumption tax.
This tax is 8% on food and nonalcoholic drinks, and 10% on most other products.
But since November 1, visitors have had to pay this tax when they buy things, even at tax-free shops.
However, they can get this money back at a later time.
When they're ready to leave Japan, they can complete a customs check to get back the tax they'd paid via credit card or another payment method.
Tourists can only claim refunds on products they take out of Japan themselves — and they must do so within 90 days of buying them.
However, the previous 500,000 yen ({{prn:$3,200|three thousand and two hundred dollars}}) spending limit on consumable products, such as food and cosmetics, has been removed.
The changes come after growing concerns that some tourists had been buying products tax-free and then reselling them within Japan.
As tourism in Japan has grown, tax-free shopping has become a much bigger business.
According to data from the Japan Tourism Agency, in 2025, foreign visitors spent around 9.5 trillion yen — or $60 billion — in Japan.
This was almost three times as much as 10 years earlier.
And as tourists spend more, the amount of tax they don't have to pay has also become a topic of debate.
In 2025, some Japanese politicians even considered ending tax-free shopping for tourists completely, after tax exemptions reached around 200 billion yen, or $1.2 billion, in 2024.
But Japanese retail groups disagreed.
They argued that ending the system could make Japan less attractive to international visitors and hurt businesses that depend on tourist spending.
For now, tax-free shopping hasn't disappeared in Japan.
Tourists can still save money — but they have to pay the tax first and claim it back later.

articles.title: 31% of Japan's Graduates Quit Jobs Within 3 Years
articles.intro: Explore why many young Japanese graduates leave their jobs within three years, changing attitudes toward lifetime employment, and related workforce trends.

sentences.text: In Japan, it was once common for people to work at the same company for their whole career.
This tradition, known as _shushin koyo_, or "lifetime employment," became popular after World War II.
Companies offered workers secure jobs, and workers often stayed until they retired.
But lifetime employment is no longer as common as it once was, and these days, many young Japanese workers leave their jobs after just a few years.
According to a new government survey, 31% of people who graduated from university in March 2023 left their jobs within three years.
And in some industries, the number was much higher.
For example, 50% of university graduates working in the accommodation and food services sector left within three years.
And in education, it was 42%.
Company size also made a big difference.
At large companies with at least 1,000 workers, about one in four young employees left within three years.
But at companies with fewer than five workers, almost 60% of employees left.
And it's not just university graduates — 37% of high school graduates also left their jobs within three years.
However, the survey also found that fewer young people are leaving their jobs than before.
In fact, this is the second year the number has fallen.
One reason may be that companies are trying harder to keep their employees.
As Japan's population gets older, there are fewer workers available, so some companies are offering higher pay and better working conditions to encourage people to stay.
Japan's tradition of lifetime employment may no longer be as common as it once was, but companies are still finding ways to encourage young workers to stay longer.

articles.title: Accent Change May Be Sign of a Good Ear — Study
articles.intro: Explore a study on how people’s accents can change when exposed to others and what this reveals about listening skills and language perception.

sentences.text: If you spend time with someone who speaks with a different accent than you, you may start to sound like them.
Or they may start to sound like you!
But no matter how much time you spend together, you both probably won't sound exactly the same — and researchers aren't sure why.
A new study looked at 136 people who speak English with an American accent.
They were first asked to read a list of words aloud.
Next, they were told to listen to a recording of a woman saying the same words with an Australian accent.
The participants were then asked to read the words aloud again.
However, they received three different types of instructions.
Some were told to read in their normal accent.
Some were told to imitate the Australian speaker as closely as possible.
And some received no instruction.
The results showed that people could copy the Australian accent when asked to.
And when told to speak normally, most people kept their American accent.
However, those who received no instruction tended to copy just one part of the Australian accent — dropping the "r" sound in certain words.
Participants were also asked what they noticed about the woman's accent.
The most common answers were the way she pronounced the letter "r," and the vowel sound in words like "bath."
The researchers found that participants who noticed these sounds tended to copy them more.
This was true whether they had been asked to imitate the woman or had received no instructions.

"Basically, if we don't tell you whether or not to imitate somebody, you're going to sound like them on the bits that you notice or think are interesting," researcher Kathryn Campbell-Kibler explained.
So maybe if your accent changes more than others', it means your ears notice those differences more!

articles.title: Most People Expect AI to Reduce Jobs for Humans
articles.intro: This lesson explores global opinions on AI's impact on jobs and society, highlighting concerns about job loss and growing economic inequality.

sentences.text: As AI becomes an increasingly common tool, there has been a lot of debate over how it will affect people's lives — and jobs — around the world.
One big question is whether AI will create jobs for humans or reduce them.
And surveys done by Pew Research Center earlier this year found that people in 34 out of 37 countries believe that AI is more likely to reduce human jobs than it is to create new ones.
Australians and South Koreans are most likely to believe that AI will result in job losses, with 76% of survey respondents in both countries saying it will lead to fewer jobs over the next 20 years.
In the US, 71% of respondents have the same opinion.
Of all the countries surveyed, only Nigerians seem slightly more optimistic than pessimistic, with 27% saying AI will lead to more new jobs, compared to 26% saying it will result in fewer jobs.
However, 30% also say they aren't sure what effect AI will have.
They aren't alone either.
In some countries, many people say they're unsure what AI means for the job market.
In the Philippines, 54% say they aren't sure, as do 49% in Thailand and 42% in Kenya.
Outside of just job losses or job creation, the world's feelings about AI use in daily life are mixed.
Across all 37 countries surveyed by Pew, an average of 37% of people are more concerned about AI than excited by it — but 41% are both concerned and excited at the same time!
Only people in Israel are more excited than concerned.
Globally, people are also more likely to say AI will increase the gap between rich and poor, with 28% saying AI will increase that gap, versus 5% saying AI will shrink it.
However, 26% also think it won't make much difference — and 36% aren't sure.

articles.title: Getting a Ticket for Machu Picchu Is Now a Little Easier
articles.intro: This lesson covers recent changes to the Machu Picchu ticket system that make booking tickets easier and more efficient for travelers.

sentences.text: Machu Picchu is a bucket-list destination for many travelers — but tickets often sell out months in advance.

However, a recent change by Peru's Ministry of Culture may make things a bit easier for travelers wanting to visit the famous Inca ruins — by making it harder for others to sit on tickets they won't actually pay for.
Previously, visitors could reserve tickets on the official website for up to three hours without paying.
These unpaid reservations temporarily blocked tickets from being bought by other people.
This meant that tickets could appear to be sold out months in advance, even if many hadn't actually been paid for.
But now, tickets can only be held for 15 minutes.
After that, if tickets haven't been paid for, the reservation is cancelled and the tickets go back on sale.
Visitors also need to provide their full name and passport number at the time of booking, and show their passport in person when they visit Machu Picchu.
It might seem like a small change, but officials think it will make a big difference.
Recent government data showed that, out of over 200,000 reservations made by tour companies, 63% were later canceled.
This meant thousands of tickets appeared to be unavailable, and anyone trying to buy a ticket would not have been able to find one.
The system is being trialed for now, and the 15-minute time limit may change.
However, the ministry said it's already noticed a huge difference since the trial began on September 22.
Earlier in September, tickets seemed to be fully booked until December.
Once the trial began, more than 90,000 tickets were freed up.
Importantly, this doesn't change the number of tickets that are sold each day — tickets are still limited to 5,600 a day during the high season from June to November, and 4,500 during low season.

Those hoping to work for very large companies also spend more than the average.
The survey also found that 33% of participants get financial help from their families to cover these costs.
Another 30% use money they get from part-time jobs or other work.
When asked what kind of support would help them most, a quarter said they want financial help with certification and language test costs.

articles.title: Coral Reefs Face Collapse in Next 50 Years, Say Experts
articles.intro: Experts warn that coral reefs worldwide face collapse in the next 50 years due to ocean warming, but actions can help protect and restore them.

sentences.text: Coral reefs support a quarter of all marine species, provide food and income for coastal communities, and help protect shorelines from storms.
But nearly all of the world's shallow-water coral reef ecosystems face a high risk of collapse by 2075, mainly because of warming oceans and heat waves.
That's the warning from a new assessment by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN).
It examined reefs across 127 tropical and subtropical regions and classified 96% of these ecosystems as critically endangered — its highest threat category.
These include Australia's Great Barrier Reef and the Red Sea's coral reefs.
The findings reflect both damage already observed and the effects of projected ocean warming.
So how does warmer water threaten these underwater communities?
When water gets too warm, corals can lose the tiny algae living in their tissues that provide much of their food.
That makes them turn white, a process called bleaching.
Corals can recover, but prolonged heat stress can kill them.
As heat waves become more frequent, reefs may have less time to recover before the next one strikes.
When a reef ecosystem collapses, its hard corals largely disappear, leaving algae, rubble and sponges in their place.
The reef can no longer support the rich variety of marine life that once depended on it.
However, being critically endangered doesn't mean a reef has already collapsed.
Most still have living coral, and researchers say there is still time to help them recover.
"The risk of coral reef collapse is escalating, but this must be a wake-up call rather than a cause for despair," said Mishal Gudka, the assessment's scientific lead.
Cutting greenhouse gas emissions is essential to limiting further warming.
But local action matters too: reducing pollution and overfishing, protecting reefs and restoring damaged areas can give them a better chance of survival.

articles.intro: Learn about Voxel, a new robot butler designed to do household chores, help you find lost items, and make home life more convenient.

sentences.text: Imagine if you could have your own personal assistant — someone to keep your home tidy, bring you cups of coffee and remind you where you left your keys.
Wouldn't that be nice?
Well, that's exactly what Tuesday Labs, a robotics company in New York, is offering with its newest creation: Voxel.
Voxel, which Tuesday Labs describes as a "droid butler," is designed to perform daily tasks around the house.
A video released by the company shows the robot sweeping up crumbs, watering plants, bringing its owner a musical instrument — and even dancing along to the music!
Voxel can also help you find things.
If you can't find your keys, for example, ask Voxel, and it will tell you where it last saw them.
Rosalind Shinkle, CEO of Tuesday Labs, told design magazine _Dezeen_ that part of her reason for creating Voxel was because she hates cleaning!
However, she also wanted to build a robot that would be nice to live with.
Robots that look too much like humans can feel a little creepy, so Tuesday Labs worked with a former character designer from Pixar to create a friendly-looking robot that doesn't look human at all.
Instead of having a head, Voxel has a simple face on its body — two animated eyes above a line for a mouth.
Its body is covered in a colorful and lightweight plastic shell, and hidden cameras allow it to find its way around the home.
Voxel stands about as tall as a kitchen counter, but its legs allow it to adjust its height to reach tables and shelves.
Tuesday Labs plans to start delivering Voxel in 2028, and the robot is expected to cost around {{prn:$20,000|twenty thousand dollars}}.
However, the company hopes to make more affordable robots in the future.

articles.title: Young Adults Find It Difficult to Make Friends — Survey
articles.intro: Explore why many young adults in the US find it difficult to make friends, based on survey results and social factors affecting connections.

sentences.text: As kids, making a friend was as easy as sitting next to somebody in class, or playing a game together on the playground.
But it's not the same for adults.
In fact, a survey has found that 69% of US young adults feel lonelier than they ever thought they would.
The survey was done by Talker Research, and included 1,000 Gen Z participants — defined as those born between 1997 and 2008.
It found that the average participant feels lonely four days a week, and 52% find it difficult to make new connections.
Forty-three percent of participants said they have fewer than three close friends.
And one in six said they only see those friends a few times a year.
So why are US young adults struggling to make friends?
Many said it's because going out and meeting people is expensive.
Others said they're too tired after work, or are too busy in other parts of their lives.
The survey also found that 60% of participants think they don't have a regular place to meet people and make friends.
This is sometimes called a "third space" — a place outside the home or work where people can spend time together.
But almost 60% also said they see the place where they work out as a "third space."
And that could be something they might want to look into if they're looking to make friends.
So maybe for young adults, making friends can still be as easy as meeting people on the playground — the playground just looks a little different.

articles.title: US Parents Say Having a Baby Is Too Expensive
articles.intro: This lesson discusses how many US parents feel the cost of raising a child is too high and explores their views on possible solutions.

sentences.text: A new baby is a cause for happiness and celebration.
But a baby also comes with large costs, from diapers and formula to car seats and childcare.
A survey by the University of Michigan found that four out of five American parents think the cost of having a baby is now just too high.
The survey included around 2,000 US adults who are parents of at least one child aged zero to 18.
Nearly all parents included in the survey agreed that early development is important to a child's long-term health.
However, giving a child what they need at a young age has often meant parents need to cut their spending, work extra hours or use secondhand items.

The survey found that parents of younger children are especially affected by the cost of having kids, with two in five describing their family's financial situation as either "struggling" or "just getting by."
And 37% of parents in these two groups said they worry about money all the time.

A lot of parents of older children haven't forgotten how difficult the first few years can be though, with 38% saying they have donated to organizations to help families with young children in the past two years.
Many parents would also support government programs to make things easier for new parents.
Three in four support the idea of a state program to give paid leave during pregnancy and during the first few weeks or months of a baby's life.

Six in 10 also said they would support programs to give families in need baby formula or healthy food, while more than half support the idea of free or lower-cost childcare, as well as free car seats and diapers.

articles.title: The Story of Mexico's _Dia de los Muertos_
articles.intro: Explore the history, traditions, and cultural significance of Mexico’s Día de los Muertos, including its indigenous and Spanish influences.

sentences.text: Orange flowers fill the streets, candles light up family altars and sugar skulls appear in shops — this is Mexico's _Dia de los Muertos_, or "Day of the Dead."
People often confuse this celebration with Halloween, but the Day of the Dead has its own unique traditions and history.
It takes place over two days — typically November 1 and November 2 — and it's a time to honor deceased loved ones.
This holiday has roots in Indigenous traditions that may date as far back as the Olmec civilization over 3,000 years ago.

These early practices were passed down through later civilizations like the Maya and the Toltecs until they reached the Aztecs — who believed that, after death, the soul travels to an underworld called Mictlan.
This journey could be long and difficult, and the dead needed help from their loved ones to reach Mictlan.
Families would leave offerings of food, water and personal belongings when a loved one died, to help guide the spirits and honor them.
In the 16th century, Spanish colonizers arrived in Mexico, bringing with them new religious traditions.
In Catholicism, November 1 is All Saints' Day — a day to honor all the saints who have reached heaven — while November 2 is All Souls' Day, a day to remember and pray for people who have died.
Over time, elements of these different traditions came together, making _Dia de los Muertos_ an important part of Mexican culture.
Every year in towns and cities across Mexico, the streets are decorated with flowers and skeletons, and people paint their faces to look like skulls.
Many families build _ofrendas_ in their homes or by the graves of their loved ones.
An _ofrenda_ is a type of altar decorated with candles, flowers and photos of the deceased, as well as some of their favorite items and foods.

Families believe these offerings help welcome the spirits of their loved ones back for a visit, making _Dia de los Muertos_ a celebration of life and the memories that keep people connected, even after death.

articles.title: One in Four European Pilots Fly When Tired
articles.intro: Explore survey findings on European airline pilots flying while fatigued, the risks involved, and the impact of company culture on safety reporting.

sentences.text: Getting through a workday feeling tired can be difficult for anyone.
But for airline pilots, it can become a serious safety issue.
A new survey of about 7,200 European pilots found that nearly one in four usually keep flying even when they feel too tired to work.
The survey was done by aviation safety company Baines Simmons for the European Cockpit Association.
It found that fatigue is a common problem across European airlines, with little change since 2023, when a similar survey was done.
More than three-quarters of pilots said they'd had at least one "microsleep" while flying in the past four weeks, with one-quarter saying they'd had five or more.
A microsleep is a very short, unintentional moment of sleep.
Not getting enough rest is a big part of the problem.

Thirty-nine percent of pilots said they "usually" or "always" had too little rest to stop fatigue from building up, while more than half said they had flown in the past three months and later realized they should have reported themselves too tired to fly.
In fact, only 37% said they usually let management know when they feel too tired to fly.
One reason may be fear of how airlines will react.
Almost half of pilots said they had flown while fatigued because they were worried about reactions from management.
The survey also found big differences between airlines and countries, with pilots at low-cost airlines reporting more problems.

Those working for airlines in Ireland and Malta were among the most likely to fear negative reactions from management, while Finland and the Netherlands had some of the strongest fatigue-reporting cultures.
The European Cockpit Association said airlines and aviation authorities need to do more to reduce fatigue risks, instead of leaving pilots to manage them on their own.

articles.title: What Do British People Complain About Most?
articles.intro: Explore what British people complain about most in public, from rude behavior to everyday annoyances and survey findings.

sentences.text: What annoys you most when you're out in public?
People being rude?
Someone pushing ahead of you in a line?
Or perhaps someone using their phone's speaker in public?
A new survey shows that British people have a lot to complain about.
The survey, done by YouGov, asked more than 2,000 people across the UK what bothers them about other people when they're in public.
The biggest complaint was people being rude to shop and restaurant workers, which annoys 67% of people who took the survey.
People who don't wait their turn in a line came second, at 59%.
Other common problems included people using their phone speakers in public, people taking up too much space on streets or buses and trains, and people making videos of themselves for social media.
But while these things bother people, they aren't actually the things they complain about most.
In fact, when asked what they complain about most in everyday life, 24% chose things they see in the news.
Another 18% chose people being rude — so that's on both lists — while 11% chose work.
And although British people are famous for talking about the country's bad weather, only 6% said the weather was what they complain about most.
And just 8% chose traffic.
Overall, 76% said they were people who often complain, while 20% said they never do.
And of the complainers, almost half said they usually share their problems with family or a partner, instead of speaking to the person who upset them.

articles.title: Japan's Budget Restaurant Saizeriya Raises Prices
articles.intro: This lesson discusses why Japanese restaurant chain Saizeriya raised prices, including rising costs and efforts to stay affordable for customers.

sentences.text: With food prices rising around the world, finding a cheap meal isn't always easy.
But in Japan, one restaurant chain is famous for keeping its prices low.

Saizeriya, a popular Italian restaurant chain, sells its famous Milano doria for just 300 yen (about {{prn:$1.90|one dollar and ninety cents}}), while a Margherita pizza costs only 400 yen (about {{prn:$2.50|two dollars and fifty cents}}).
Or at least, that's what they used to cost.
But now, Saizeriya is increasing its prices for the first time in six years.
On October 29, Saizeriya prices increased by an average of 6%, and some restaurants increased prices by as much as 10%.
It's the company's first general price increase since 1998.
Saizeriya did make some small changes in 2020, but those were intended to reduce the need for coins and change during the COVID-19 pandemic.
Over the years, Saizeriya has found different ways to save money and keep its prices low.
For example, it has its own vegetable farms and factories, and has even tried using robots to serve food.
But these efforts are no longer enough, as higher food and energy costs have made it difficult to avoid price increases.
At a press conference in October, Saizeriya CEO Hideharu Matsutani said the price increase was "regrettable."
But after hearing the announcement, many people shared messages on social media in support of Saizeriya.

One customer told _The Japan Times_ that Saizeriya's meals have been so cheap that eating there can cost less than cooking at home, and that most people are just surprised the company has kept its prices so low for so long.
And even with the higher prices, Saizeriya still wants to keep its food affordable.
At the press conference, Matsutani said that if the company finds another way to make meals cheaper, he'll take it.

articles.title: Young Japanese Have Worse Diets than Older Japanese
articles.intro: This lesson explores a study comparing the diets of young and older Japanese people, highlighting health, nutrition, and lifestyle factors.

sentences.text: A new study has found that young adults in Japan often have less healthy diets than older people in the country.
Researchers from the University of Tokyo did a study with about 4,500 people in Japan.
The people were as old as 79, and as young as just 1.
The researchers asked them — or their parents — to write down what they ate and drank for eight days.
Then, they gave them diet scores.
The researchers looked at two things: the foods people ate, like fruit and vegetables, and the nutrients they got, like vitamins.
Men who were around 23 years old, and women who were around 16, had the lowest scores for the foods they ate.
After that, their scores got better almost every year they got older.
For nutrients, both men's and women's scores went up until around age 10.
But then they went down quickly, until they were at their lowest around age 24.
After that, nutrient scores started slowly going up again.
The study also found that people from families with more money and education had healthier diets.
And smokers and people who skip breakfast in the morning had less healthy diets.
The researchers said teens and young adults may find it harder to eat well because their lives are changing so much at that age.
But they said it's important to teach young people how to eat healthily.

articles.intro: This lesson discusses the planned price increases for some Shinkansen (bullet train) tickets in Japan starting in 2027 due to inflation.

sentences.text: Japan's bullet trains — the Shinkansen — are known for being fast, comfortable and convenient.
But passengers may soon have to pay more to travel on them.
Central Japan Railway Company (JR Central) and West Japan Railway Company (JR West) have announced plans to increase the prices of some tickets in 2027.
The Nozomi and Mizuho trains are Japan's fastest bullet trains, making the fewest stops between their starting and ending stations.
During busy periods, passengers can only buy tickets for these trains if they pay for reserved seats.

From July 2027, tickets for reserved seats will increase by between 10 yen — about 6 cents — and {{prn:880|eight hundred and eighty}} yen — about {{prn:$5.60|five dollars and sixty cents}} — depending on the route.
For example, the route between Tokyo Station and Shin-Osaka Station will increase by 700 yen, or about {{prn:$4.40|four dollars and forty cents}}.
The new price will be {{prn:6,510 |six thousand five hundred and ten}} yen, or about {{prn:$41|forty one dollars}}.

And reserved seats on the train between Tokyo and Nagoya will increase to  {{prn:11,880|eleven thousand eight hundred and eighty}} yen — about {{prn:$75|seventy five dollars}} — up from {{prn:11,300|eleven thousand and three hundred}} yen, or about {{prn:$71|seventy one dollars}}.
JR Central and JR West also plan to increase ticket prices for their first-class seats — Green Car seats — in December 2027.
Green Car tickets on Nozomi trains between Tokyo and Shin-Osaka will increase by {{prn:3,700|three thousand and seven hundred}} yen, or about {{prn:$23.40|twenty three dollars and forty cents}}.
They'll rise by {{prn:4,080 |four thousand and eighty}} yen, or about {{prn:$25.70|twenty five dollars and seventy cents}}, on Mizuho trains between Shin-Osaka and Hakata.

articles.title: These Symptoms Send Japanese People to the Doctor
articles.intro: Explore survey results on the symptoms that most often send Japanese people to the doctor and their use of over-the-counter medicine.

sentences.text: Would you go to the doctor if you had a headache or a cold?
What about if you had a high fever or a bad rash?
Tokyo company Intage Healthcare asked people in Japan questions about what they do when they get sick.
The survey included more than 2,500 people aged between 16 and 79.
Participants were given a list of 32 conditions and, for each condition, were asked how likely they were to visit a doctor if they had symptoms.
Eighty-four percent of participants said they would go to the doctor if they had a high fever.
Fifty-seven percent said they would go to the doctor if they had chronic headaches, while 55% said they would go if they had a rash.
These were the top three symptoms that would send people to a doctor.
Participants were also asked questions about their use of over-the-counter (OTC) medicine.

The results showed that participants are most likely to use OTC medicine for things like occasional headaches, colds, sore throats and low fevers — though as a fever gets above 38 degrees Celsius, people are more likely to see a doctor.
Many said they take OTC medicine because it helps them feel better, while others said it's because they often have it at home and it's easier and quicker than going to the doctor.
However, more than 30% said they often choose to rest and wait for symptoms to go away on their own, instead of taking medicine.

articles.title: How to Carve the Perfect Halloween Pumpkin
articles.intro: Learn about the history and step-by-step process of carving the perfect Halloween pumpkin, including helpful tips and tricks.

sentences.text: The tradition of carving a scary face in a pumpkin is believed to have been started by Irish immigrants in the US — who, when in Ireland, would carve scary faces on turnips.
The idea was that the faces would frighten away spirits.
But how do you carve the perfect pumpkin?
First, get a large, fresh pumpkin with a flat bottom.
You can buy it early, but don't carve it until about three days before Halloween.
Start by cutting a big hole in the top with a sharp knife.
Cut at an angle, so the cut piece doesn't fall into the pumpkin when you put it back on.
Some people prefer to cut the bottom, saying it's safer to put a pumpkin over a lit candle than to put your hand inside to light it.
Then, use a big spoon to take out the soft inside of the pumpkin.
To make it easier to carve, it's best to make the pumpkin wall thinner on one side — _Good Housekeeping_ recommends leaving it about 3 centimeters thick.
You could also use the wall parts to make soup, or cook the seeds for a snack.
Next, draw a face on the pumpkin using a pen, then cut it out with a knife.
You could also draw your idea on paper first, then use a fork to make holes in the pumpkin along the lines you want to cut.
Finally, put a light inside — an artificial candle is usually safest.
If your pumpkin starts looking tired before October 31, you can put its face in cold water for a few hours to make it look fresh again.
